body:
Picking up bd-01KZYYQCR3D7NDZQN5DN53AHRC, the rdm_sampling_covariance cost bead, which I did not file. I tested its three hypotheses separately. Two are ruled out, the third is confirmed and quantified, and the answer changes the fix.

FIRST, MY OWN MISS. I had direct evidence of this and did not act on it. My coverage verification of the same function ran 600 calls and blew a 600-second timeout; I wrote 'slow' in my notes and treated it as the honest cost of a new capability. Whoever filed this was looking where I was not.

NOT A LEAK. Twelve sequential calls on one plan: mean of first three 0.963 s, mean of last three 1.016 s, ratio 1.05x, correlation of call index with time +0.084. RSS rose 313 to 373 MB then fell to 284 MB, net minus 30 MB, correlation +0.109. That is garbage collection working. A leak may still exist at 577 nodes, but it is not needed to explain the observation.

NOT DRIVEN BY CONDITION COUNT. The natural guess is that q=8 is expensive because Eq. 13 is a D x D covariance with D = 28:

  q    D pairs   secs/node   secs per pair
  2          1       1.448          1.4477
  4          6       1.050          0.1749
  6         15       0.978          0.0652
  8         28       0.992          0.0354

Flat in q. At q=8 a node costs about 1 s here, not 7 s.

IT IS FRAME-SIZE DRIVEN. Holding q and support roughly constant, varying only node count:

  nodes    secs/node
  40           0.704
  80           0.487
  160          0.874
  320          1.729

Four times the nodes gives three and a half times the per-node cost. Roughly linear.

SO A FULL MAP SWEEP IS QUADRATIC IN NODE COUNT. N nodes each costing O(N) is O(N^2), which reproduces the field observation with no leak at all. Extrapolated to 577 nodes that is roughly half an hour before accounting for the larger supports, same order as the reported hour.

The bead already suspected 'per-call recomputation of plan/fit-invariant work'. That is right, and the sharpening is that the recomputed work scales with the FRAME rather than being fixed overhead. It also explains why the certified scale benchmark missed it: at a single node the redundant work is invisible by construction, so the benchmark could not have caught this no matter how large the node was.

CAVEATS, because I have over-claimed from timing twice today. Synthetic data, 40-320 voxels, supports of 6-8 features, far from 577 nodes at 50 voxels. The 80-node point is faster than the 40-node point, so there is real noise. And I did not identify which invariant work is redone - that wants profiling inside the call, and the implementer is better placed.

Suggested next step: profile one call at two frame sizes and diff by function. Whatever grows between them is the object to precompute once and share, which is the first fix shape the bead already proposes.

Separately: the exemplars/haxby2001 directory is the worked example five of my beads independently asked for, and 03-rmvpa-searchlight.R plus 04-compare.R is a head-to-head against the incumbent that nothing in my review suggested and that is worth more than most of what I did suggest.
